q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b.name AS beer, MIN(s.price) AS price, s.bar FROM beer AS b LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.beer LEFT JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS lowest_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS lp ON b.name = lp.beer AND s.price = lp.lowest_price GROUP BY b.name, s.bar ORDER BY b.name, s.bar

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they handle the join conditions differently. Q1 joins the 'serves' table twice, while Q2 joins it only once with a subquery. This difference can lead to different results, especially when there are multiple rows in the 'serves' table for the same beer and bar.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a beer served by multiple bars at different prices. The difference in join conditions between Q1 and Q2 should cause Q1 to return more results than Q2.
